I've been farming these 10 mu for 30 years. Me and my wife, we do the work ourselves. I never went to school, but I know this land better than any book. My father taught me, and I learned with my own hands.

**Wheat — same as always**

I plant winter wheat on all 10.1 mu in early October. I buy improved seed from the shop — about 12 kg per mu, two and a half big scoops. Costs a bit, but saved seed doesn't grow as good after a few years. Before planting, I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer on each mu. That's the 40 kg bag from the shop. I know it's about right because I've done it for 20 years. Then at Qingming, when the wheat starts jointing, I spread half a bag of urea — about 20 kg per mu. If the wheat looks yellow, I might add a little more, but usually half a bag is enough. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat doesn't freeze, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Water costs money for pumping, so I don't waste it, but you can't skip it either. One spray of herbicide after planting — the shopkeeper knows which one, I just point to the bottle I got last year. I hire the combine for harvest in early June. I'm 53, my back isn't what it was, and the machine is faster. That costs about 50 yuan per mu.

**Maize — no time to rest**

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we plant the maize. The window is tight — sometimes only a few days. I use hybrid seed, about 2 jin per mu. You have to buy hybrid every year, can't save it. When planting, I put fertilizer in the furrow — about half a bag of compound per mu and some urea, maybe 15 kg. Maize doesn't need as much fuss as wheat. I irrigate twice if it's dry, especially when it's tasseling. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu for maize, and about 800 jin for wheat. I expect about the same this year if the weather holds.

**Money and labor**

We don't have much cash lying around. Every yuan I spend on fertilizer is a yuan I can't use if someone gets sick. So I don't buy the fancy stuff, and I don't experiment. What worked last year will work this year. Me and my wife do most of the work — spreading fertilizer, spraying, irrigating. We might hire a couple of days' help during the busy times, and the combine for wheat. Total spend for the year is probably around 5,000 yuan. That's a lot for us, but we have to put food on the table.
